extracted.intended_audience: Host organisations, IMO Board members, national team Leaders and Deputy Leaders, coordinators, contestants and observers
extracted.subtask_description: The formal rules governing organisation and participation in the International Mathematical Olympiad, covering governance, eligibility, problem proposals, contest conduct, jury and coordination procedures, accommodation, prizes, sanctions and force majeure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence of regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The IMO is governed by the General Regulations together with the Annual Regulations and the Articles of Association; the Annual Regulations take precedence over the General Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual Regulations specify details specific to each IMO or required by national law and supersede General Regulations where they conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Country and Host Organisation designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An IMO takes place on dates and in a Host Country specified in the Annual Regulations; a Host Organisation specified in the Annual Regulations has overall responsibility for the organisation of an IMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Host Organisation must ensure arrangements support the aims of the IMO and competition in the spirit of fair play and may approve extensions of deadlines specified in the Annual Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims of the IMO
rubrics_metrics.description: to discover, encourage and challenge mathematically gifted young people in all countries; to foster friendly international relationships among mathematicians of all countries; to create an opportunity for the exchange of information on school syllabuses and practices throughout the world; to promote mathematics generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMO Board powers and co-opted members
rubrics_metrics.description: The IMO Board makes recommendations to the Jury regarding future IMOs and acts on behalf of the Jury between IMOs; it may appoint up to three co-opted members to strengthen capacity, by majority vote of appointed members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-opted members may be appointed at any time, serve up to four years, may stand for election or be re-appointed, and have voting rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of General Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Regulations may be amended, for future IMOs, by resolution of the Jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of Annual Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annual Regulations for an IMO must be approved by the IMO Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Country contribution to IMO Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Host Country of an IMO must contribute at least USD 5000 to the IMO Foundation towards ongoing infrastructure costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official languages
rubrics_metrics.description: The official languages of the IMO are English, French, German, Russian and Spanish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The IMO must be free from bullying, sexual harassment and any other form of discrimination; all participants must conduct themselves with dignity and show respect to everyone; no one may take advantage of the IMO for political purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IMO Ethics Committee will investigate allegations and may sanction individuals (including requiring them to leave and barring future attendance); persons may appeal to elected IMO Board members whose decision is final. Host Country laws take precedence and serious misconduct will be reported to police.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation by invitation and team composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation is by invitation only. Each invited country/territory is entitled to send a team of up to six contestants, a Leader and a Deputy Leader; a team must have a Leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no Deputy Leader, the Leader follows the Official Programme for Deputy Leaders and does not receive the Shortlist or form part of the Jury until after the Contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestant age and enrollment eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must have been born on or after 1 July in the year x−20 where x is the year of participation, and must have been normally enrolled in full-time primary or secondary education on or after 1 December in the year prior to the IMO; home-schooled students must not have received a high-school diploma and must be working toward such a credential on 1 December.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and long-term residency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants should normally be citizens of the Country they represent, but genuine long-term foreign residents being educated in that Country may be permitted if they have spent at least one full academic year there and will spend a total of at least two years in full-time education there before leaving secondary education, and the foreign education is for a bona fide family reason, not to change national IMO status artificially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMO tourism is not permitted: a student may not attempt the final selection examinations of more than one country in a given IMO year. The Board may approve deviations in exceptional circumstances and will publish reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observers categories and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers (including family) may apply to accompany Participants as Observer A (with Leaders), Observer B (with Deputy Leaders), or Observer C (with Contestants); the Annual Regulations specify charges and deadlines and no guarantee is given that applications will be successful due to limited extra accommodation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the IMO Board who are not Leaders may attend as Observer A; Host Organisation may waive charges but is not obliged to. Host Organisation should waive charges for one Observer A and one Observer B from the Host Country for the following year's IMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Programme and modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Programme is the programme and itinerary for the IMO and associated events; the Host Organisation reserves the right to amend or revise it and should notify Participants and Observers of significant changes and obtain IMO Board approval before making significant changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Programme contains accommodation and venue details; the detailed Official Programme may not be disclosed until arrival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online confirmation and registration deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each invited Country must confirm participation online by the date specified in the Annual Regulations using credentials provided by the Host Organisation; this confirms the Leader agrees to abide by the regulations. Participants, Observers and travel details must be registered by specified dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders/Deputy Leaders acting in loco parentis
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders and Deputy Leaders are responsible for the conduct of Contestants and act in loco parentis except where an Observer is nominated in writing to act in loco parentis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders' responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders must inform Contestants and others of regulations (including prohibited items), ensure their Country submits problems to the Problem Selection Committee and keeps proposals secret, attend all Jury meetings and participate, inform the Jury of any shortlisted problem already known, ensure accurate translations of chosen problems for their team, meet Host Country deadlines, ensure Contestants receive fair scores consistent with marking schemes, keep contact details updated, and inform their national committee of Jury decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the Leader may submit problem proposals through a secure procedure; Leader's role includes ensuring secrecy and fair coordination outcomes for their team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deputy Leader responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Deputy Leaders should be sufficiently involved in mathematics to help the Leader and replace them in an emergency; they should assist the Leader with evaluation of solutions and coordination, inform Contestants of examination regulations, and supervise conduct and welfare of the team during IMO activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Organisation coverage of official expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Host Organisation covers all official expenses for Participants and Observers, including accommodation, meals, transport between official arrival/departure sites and accommodation sites, and other necessary transport between accommodation sites and other Official Programme venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Organisation non-liability for non-official costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than for accommodation, meals and transport during the Official Programme, the Host Organisation is not liable for any costs incurred by Participants or Observers, including extra days in the Host Country, travel to/from the Host Country, or travel within the Host Country prior to arrival at or after departure from official sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All Participants and Observers are responsible for obtaining full accident, health and travel insurance; the Leader must confirm online that this condition has been met for all Participants and Observers of their team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excursions and cultural trips
rubrics_metrics.description: The Host Organisation must offer opportunities for excursions and/or cultural trips but is under no obligation to organise specific activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation arrangements and single-room policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annual Regulations specify whether accommodation is shared or single; where shared, application for single rooms may be permitted with charges and deadlines; extra accommodation is limited and not guaranteed; no charge is made for single rooms for members of the IMO Board who are Leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem proposal submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating Country other than the Host Country is expected to submit up to six proposed problems with solutions to the Problem Selection Committee by the date in the Annual Regulations; only the Leader may submit proposals via a secure procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should cover various fields of pre-university mathematics, varying difficulty, be new, not suggested for or used in other competitions, be written in official languages and accompanied by English versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest schedule and remote examination exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contest takes place on two consecutive days specified in the Annual Regulations, each examination starts in the morning and lasts four and a half hours; each paper has three problems. The IMO exam can only be taken remotely in the event of Force Majeure (e.g. war, natural disasters). No other exceptions (health, religious reasons, etc.) are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of problems and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contestant may receive the problems in one, two or three languages requested on the registration form provided the Jury has approved the relevant translation; at least one requested language must be an official language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent work and answer form rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contestant must work independently and submit solutions in their own language on answer forms provided by the Host Organisation, writing on only one side of each answer form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted and prohibited instruments; special needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Only writing and drawing instruments (such as rulers and compasses) are permitted; books, papers, tables, calculators, protractors, computers and communication devices are not allowed. Requests for special needs will generally not be granted if they provide conditions from which other contestants could benefit (e.g., additional time, a computer for writing, separate room).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special needs unlikely to be granted when they would confer an advantage usable by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of problems, shortlist and communications during Jury period
rubrics_metrics.description: Jury, Observers and others with prior knowledge of problems and solutions must ensure no Contestant has information about any proposed problem and keep all contest problems and solutions strictly confidential until after the Contest; they are barred from external communication with Contestants, Deputy Leaders and Observers B and C from arrival at the Jury site until the conclusion of the second examination, and vice versa for Contestants and certain observers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If emergency communication becomes necessary, the Host Organisation must provide proper assistance. Information about arrivals/delays must go exclusively to the published IMO office which may forward to Leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize numbers and ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of prizes (first, second and third) must be approved by the Jury and must not exceed half the total number of Contestants unless approved by at least two thirds of the Jury; numbers of first, second and third prizes must be approximately in the ratio 1:2:3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special prizes and certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Special prizes may be awarded for solutions considered outstanding by the Jury (proposals put forward by the Chief Coordinator); prizes are awarded at the Closing Ceremony; Contestants who did not receive first/second/third but received seven points for a solution receive a Certificate of Honourable Mention; each Participant and Observer receives a Certificate of Participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication consent and anonymisation requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants and Observers consent to publication of their names and photographs on the IMO website; results may be anonymised and photographs removed on request made by a Contestant at least two years after their final participation, via the registered IMO contact for that Country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury composition and observers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jury consists of all Leaders together with a Chair; a Leader may be replaced by their Deputy Leader in an emergency (subject to Chair approval). Members of the IMO Board not on the Jury, members of the Problem Selection Committee and Coordinators may attend as observers with permission of the Chair but are not entitled to speak or vote (except at explicit request of the Chair). Deputy Leaders may attend, as observers, Jury meetings held after the Contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury voting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Jury members may vote; each Jury member has one vote. A motion is carried by a simple majority of those voting, and in the event of a tie the Chair has a casting vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury powers and duties before, during and after the Contest
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the Contest the Jury selects Contest problems from the Shortlist, verifies participant eligibility, prepares and approves official problem versions, approves translations and marking schemes. During the Contest the Jury considers written questions raised by Contestants in the first half hour and decides replies. After the Contest the Jury receives reports from the Chief Invigilator and Chief Coordinator, approves scores, decides prize winners, considers special prize proposals, and matters for future IMOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling allegations of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any allegation or suspicion of a violation must be reported to the Chair of the Jury; if there is a prima facie case, the Chair must form a committee to investigate and report to the Jury, which decides whether a violation occurred and what sanction to apply; possible sanctions include disqualification of an individual or an entire team; the Jury's decision is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Problem Shortlist must be kept strictly confidential until the conclusion of the following IMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Jury member receives the Shortlist for themselves and their Observer A on the first day of the Official Programme for Leaders or upon arrival if later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination process and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination determines official scores in a homogeneous, fair and transparent manner. Leaders must submit papers to a coordination group provided by the Host Organisation consisting of a Chief Coordinator and, for each problem, a Problem Captain and group of Coordinators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring per problem
rubrics_metrics.description: For each problem each Contestant receives an integer score out of a maximum of seven points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment prior to coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to coordination, Contestants' solutions are assessed by Leaders and Deputy Leaders and, independently, by Coordinators in accordance with marking schemes approved by the Jury; only Participants and Observers at the IMO and invited people present may see solutions before official approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders, Deputy Leaders and Observers are encouraged to assist Leaders/Deputy Leaders of other Countries in difficult solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination session participation and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each coordination session involves two Coordinators provided by the Host Organisation and representatives of the relevant Country (normally Leader and Deputy Leader) permitted to participate actively; with Chief Coordinator approval one further representative or Coordinator may observe but not take active part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Leader and designated Coordinators should agree on scores recorded on official forms and signed. Disagreements are referred to the Problem Captain, then to the Chief Coordinator, and if unresolved reported to the Jury with a recommendation. If an irregularity is suspected, Coordinators must refer immediately to the Chief Coordinator and may report to the Chair of the Jury if not satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of Host Country contestants
rubrics_metrics.description: For each problem, solutions by Contestants from the Host Country are coordinated by the Leader and Deputy Leader of the Country that submitted the problem, with assistance of the Problem Captain for that problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire agreement clause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Articles of Association, these Regulations, and the documents referred to herein constitute the full agreement and understanding of the parties and supersede any previous discussions or representations made by or on behalf of the Host Organisation in respect of an IMO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effect of force majeure
rubrics_metrics.description: Force majeure means any cause preventing the Host Organisation from performing obligations arising from acts, events or omissions beyond reasonable control, including strikes, act of God, war, riot, compliance with law, accident, breakdown, earthquake, typhoon, fire, flood, storm, or default of suppliers. If the Host Organisation is prevented or delayed by force majeure it has no liability for affected obligations during continuation and for such time after as necessary to recommence operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IMO exam may only be taken remotely in event of force majeure; no other exceptions allowed.
